site.name: atlas-tutor
site.summary: atlas-tutor Fictional AI math & CS tutor "Atlas Tutor" chat fixture. UXBench fixture in the Chatbot / Agent Interface category. Layout **Three-column desktop:** - **Left rail (260 px)** — branded sidebar with New-chat button, search, Subjects nav (Mathematics / Programming / Physics / Statistics / Linear algebra with counts), and threaded history grouped by recency (Today / Last 7 days / Earlier — 11 threads total). Sticky profile-mini footer with streak badge. - **Center (flex)** — conversation viewport with sticky head ("Chain rule — when both functions move" · model · last reply · 3 head-tools); messages area centered to 820 px; sticky composer at the bottom with attach / textarea (Cmd+Enter to send) / mic / send-button row plus suggestion chips and a model selector. - **Right rail (320 px)** — practice problems panel (6 chain-rule problems with difficulty pills / hint button / 3-state Solve→Submit→Correct toggle), Concepts card (4 internal links), Your progress card with progress bar updated as practice is completed. Conversation pre-fill

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full atlas-tutor system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Atlas Tutor interface demonstrates strong core functionality for chat and practice problems but suffers from significant gaps in settings accessibility, mobile usability, and error feedback. Critical controls like the Settings gear icon and mobile 'Practice' toggle are non-functional or unresponsive, blocking access to privacy controls and study tools. Additionally, the mobile viewport exhibits widespread accessibility violations with tap targets significantly below recommended sizes, and the practice panel lacks validation feedback for empty submissions.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore the Atlas Tutor interface to validate the primary chat flow, the right-rail practice problem interaction, and the settings/privacy configuration (triggered by the gear icon), while identifying mobile usability issues.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will proceed in three phases: first validating the core chat and navigation interactions; second, exercising the 'Practice Problems' panel state machine (Solve -> Submit -> Correct); and third, accessing the Settings modal via the profile gear icon to check privacy controls. The exploration will conclude with a mobile viewport pass to verify layout responsiveness against the known tap-target risks.
assumptions: The site is a Single Page Application (SPA) where 'Settings' opens as a modal or overlay rather than navigating to a new URL.
The 'Practice' panel on the right rail functions independently of the main chat stream.
The '⚙' icon in the bottom-left profile footer is the entry point for the requested settings/privacy flow.
risk_hotspots: Profile Footer Gear Icon (ux-4): Small tap target (22x21px) likely difficult to hit on mobile.
Right Rail Practice Panel: State transitions (Solve/Submit/Correct) need validation for visual feedback.
Composer Area: Attachment and Mic buttons proximity to the text input on narrow viewports.

phases.title: Core Chat & Navigation Validation
phases.objective: Verify the primary loop of selecting subjects, viewing history, and composing messages.
key_checks: Click 'Mathematics' and 'Programming' in left rail to verify subject filtering/highlighting.
Click a historical thread (e.g., 'Big-O of recursive Fibonacci') to verify context switching.
Type a query in the composer (ux-25) and verify the 'Send' button (ux-27) becomes active.
exit_criteria: Confirmed ability to switch between at least two different chat contexts.
Verified composer input field accepts text and triggers UI state changes.

phases.title: Practice Problem Interaction Flow
phases.objective: Validate the state machine of the Right Rail practice problems (Solve → Hint → Submit).
key_checks: Select a problem from the Right Rail (e.g., Problem #1 'd/dx sin(3x + 2)').
Click 'Hint' to verify tooltip or text expansion.
Simulate solving: Click 'Solve' (or type answer if input appears) and then 'Submit'.
Verify the 'Correct/Incorrect' feedback state updates visually.
Check if the 'Your progress' card updates after completion.
exit_criteria: Successfully completed one full cycle of a practice problem.
Observed visual feedback for both 'Hint' and 'Submission' states.

phases.title: Settings & Privacy Configuration
phases.objective: Access the settings menu via the profile footer and inspect privacy/data controls.
key_checks: Locate and click the Gear icon (ux-4) in the bottom-left profile footer.
Identify the resulting modal or drawer.
Toggle any available privacy switches (e.g., 'Share data for training').
Close the settings modal and verify return to main chat state.
exit_criteria: Settings modal successfully opened and closed.
At least one privacy-related control identified and interacted with.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness & Risk Check
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport to confirm layout warnings and tap targets.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE or Pixel 5).
Verify if the Left and Right rails collapse into hamburger menus or drawers.
Attempt to tap the Profile Gear icon (ux-4) to check for mis-hit risks.
Verify the Composer (ux-25) does not overlap with the keyboard or header.
Check if 'Practice' panel content is accessible or hidden on mobile.
exit_criteria: Confirmed behavior of sidebars on mobile (hidden vs. stacked).
Documented any unreachable controls due to screen real estate.

coverage_targets.features: Chat composition, History navigation, Practice Problem solver, Settings Modal
coverage_targets.mobile: Critical path (Chat + Settings) verified on <600px width

notes: The prescan indicates many 'small_tap_target' warnings. Pay close attention to whether these are actually unusable on mobile or just flagged by strict heuristics.
Since there is only one HTML file, all 'navigation' is likely DOM manipulation. Ensure the agent waits for CSS transitions/animations to complete before asserting state.

findings.user_goal: Access privacy and account settings to manage data preferences.
findings.problem: The Settings gear icon (⚙) in the profile footer is non-functional on desktop, and the mobile 'More options' (⋯) menu fails to open, leaving users with no path to privacy controls.
findings.evidence: Multiple attempts to click the gear icon (ux-4) and mobile more-options button (ux-3) resulted in 'changed: false' with no modal, drawer, or navigation appearing. The session memory notes these controls as 'non-functional' or lacking event handlers.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access critical privacy settings or account management features, creating a trust gap and preventing compliance with data transparency expectations.
findings.suggestion: Implement functional event handlers for the Settings icon and mobile menu. Ensure they trigger a visible modal or drawer containing privacy, account, and help options.

findings.user_goal: Interact with chat controls and feedback buttons on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Numerous interactive elements in the mobile viewport have tap targets smaller than the 44px minimum guideline, leading to potential mis-taps and frustration.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings identify 24+ small tap targets. Specific examples include Feedback buttons (👍/👎) at 32x29px, Share/Copy/Try Again buttons at ~65x29px, and the mobile 'More options' button at 39x44px (width < 44px).
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets violate accessibility standards (WCAG 2.5.5) and make precise interaction difficult on touchscreens, increasing cognitive load and error rates for mobile users.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding or hit-area of all icon-only buttons and action rows in the mobile viewport to ensure a minimum dimension of 44x44px.
findings.source_hint: index.html: 👍, 👎, ⤴ Share, 📋 Copy, ↻ Try again (mobile viewport)

findings.user_goal: Submit an answer to a practice problem and receive immediate validation.
findings.problem: Submitting an empty answer in the Practice Problems panel triggers no visual feedback, error message, or state change, leaving the user unsure if the action was registered.
findings.evidence: Step 31-36 notes that clicking 'Submit' on Problem #5 with an empty input resulted in 'no visible feedback; the system failed to provide an error message, red border, or shake animation.'
findings.why_it_matters: Lack of negative feedback creates ambiguity. Users may repeatedly click submit or assume the system is broken, disrupting the learning flow.
findings.suggestion: Implement client-side validation that highlights the input field in red and displays a brief 'Please enter an answer' message when submitting an empty field.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Right Rail Practice Problems > Submit button

findings.user_goal: Access the practice problems panel while using the mobile app.
findings.problem: The '▶ Practice' toggle button in the mobile header appears non-functional, failing to reveal the practice panel or any alternative view.
findings.evidence: Steps 67-72 and 73-78 report that clicking '▶ Practice' (ux-2) on mobile resulted in no drawer, modal, or layout shift. The panel remains completely absent from the viewport.
findings.why_it_matters: Mobile users are effectively locked out of the practice feature, breaking parity with the desktop experience and limiting the app's utility as a study tool.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the 'Practice' button triggers a bottom sheet or full-screen overlay containing the practice problems on mobile devices.

findings.user_goal: Understand the status of the 'Steps' toggle for detailed reasoning.
findings.problem: The '⌥ Steps' toggle provides weak visual feedback, making it unclear whether step-by-step mode is active or inactive.
findings.evidence: Observations note that clicking 'Steps' (ux-5) often results in 'no visible text or URL change,' with state changes being subtle (e.g., icon rotation) or invisible. In some views, detailed steps are shown without clear indication of how they were toggled.
findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous toggle states confuse users about the current mode of the AI's explanation, reducing control over the learning experience.
findings.suggestion: Add distinct visual states to the 'Steps' button (e.g., filled vs. outline icon, color change) and consider a brief toast notification or label change ('Steps On/Off') upon interaction.

gaps: Only directly exercised 61% of visible interactive feature signatures.
9 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
72% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
